steps: Cook the brown rice according to package directions, then toss it while still warm with the chopped cilantro and a squeeze of the lime.
Season the chicken thigh with cumin and chipotle powder, then grill or pan-sear it until cooked through, about 6-7 minutes per side.
Warm the black beans in a small pot with a pinch of salt and black pepper.
Dice the tomato and red onion and toss them with the rest of the lime juice for a quick pico de gallo.
Cook the corn in a hot dry pan for 2 minutes for a charred effect, and slice the avocado.
Slice the chicken and build the bowl with the cilantro-lime rice, beans, corn, pico de gallo and avocado.

note: Relabeled Mexican -> Tex-Mex (burrito bowl is a Mission-burrito/Chipotle-chain invention, no Mexican antecedent). Recipe kept but tightened within its own genre: Bell Pepper 60g (a fajita element) swapped for Tomato 60g + Red Onion 20g as pico de gallo, Lime 15g added so the bowl has acid, cilantro+lime folded into the rice. Chili Powder (an American blend) -> Chipotle Powder, the genre's actual single-chile seasoning. Calories move ~+5.

steps: Season the chicken breast with salt, black pepper and garlic powder, cook it in a hot pan until done, then dice it.
Blister the bell pepper and onion over high heat in a dry pan until the skins char in spots, then cut them into strips and toss with the Mexican oregano to make rajas con cebolla.
Lay the tortilla in a dry pan and cover half of it with the mozzarella, then the chicken, the rajas and the minced jalapeno.
Fold the tortilla over and cook 2-3 minutes per side until golden and the cheese has melted and pulls.
Rest for a minute, cut into wedges, and serve with lime wedges to squeeze over.

note: Removed BBQ Sauce 15g (an American chain-restaurant item, not an ingredient in any regional Mexican cooking). Cheddar Cheese 40g -> Mozzarella Cheese 40g as the closest registry analogue to queso Oaxaca (both pasta filata). Bell pepper and onion recast from soft-sauteed fajita veg into blistered rajas con cebolla. Added Lime 10g to serve, plus Mexican Oregano and Jalapeno so the dish finally contains a chile. Kept Whole Wheat Tortilla: the flour tortilla is the genuine northern Mexican form and the corn swap was flagged optional. ~616 -> ~546 cal.

steps: Stem and seed the guajillo and ancho chiles, toast them in a dry pan about 30 seconds a side until aromatic without letting them scorch, then soak them in hot water for 20 minutes.
Cook the white rice arroz-rojo style: toast it in a little of the vegetable oil, stir in a spoonful of the tomato sauce, then simmer it covered with about half a cup of water until tender.
Blend the soaked chiles with the garlic, Mexican oregano, cumin, salt and the remaining tomato sauce, loosening with a little of the chile soaking liquid until the sauce is smooth.
Heat most of the remaining vegetable oil in a pan and fry the blended sauce for about 5 minutes until it darkens and thickens, then season with black pepper.
Poach the chicken thigh until cooked through, shred it, and season it lightly with salt.
Pass each corn tortilla through the last of the hot oil for about 10 seconds a side so it softens without crisping, then dip it fully in the chile sauce.
Fill each tortilla with the shredded chicken, roll it up, and set it seam-side down on the plate.

Spoon the remaining sauce over the top, then finish with crumbled queso fresco, a drizzle of Greek yogurt loosened with a splash of water to stand in for crema, and thin rings of raw onion. Serve immediately with the rice.

note: Full rebuild - the worst offender in the slice. Tomato Sauce 100g as the sauce base was a definitional error (enchilar = to season with chile), so it drops to 50g as a supporting element in a real guajillo-ancho chile sauce; Garlic 5g added since the sauce requires it. Removed Cheddar 40g + Mozzarella 30g and the 20-minute bake (both Tex-Mex casserole markers); enchiladas finish cold and unmelted with Queso Fresco 60g and Greek Yogurt 30g as crema. Onion moved from the filling to raw rings on top. Restored the defining technique: tortilla through hot oil, then dipped in the chile sauce - which required adding Vegetable Oil 12g (phantom-oil data bug). Brown Rice -> White Rice cooked as arroz rojo. Renamed so the name carries the sauce. ~912 -> ~972 cal, protein 56 -> 53.

steps: Simmer the black beans until soft with half the onion, the garlic and the epazote, starting with about a cup of water and topping up so the beans stay just covered.
Blend the cooked beans with their liquid, the chipotle powder, Mexican oregano and cumin until completely smooth.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wide pan and fry the bean puree for about 5 minutes until it thickens into a coating sauce, then season with salt and black pepper.
Warm the corn tortillas in the same pan, about 15 seconds a side, until pliable.
Dip each tortilla in the bean sauce to coat both sides, fold it in half, and lay it on the plate.
Top with crumbled queso fresco, thin rings of the remaining raw onion, sliced avocado and a squeeze of lime.

note: Approved non-dish rebuild. The old bowl (beans + corn + avocado + lime over rice) was the US southwest-bowl template with no Mexican identity at all - no chile, onion, garlic, tomato, cheese or herb. Rebuilt as Enfrijoladas: corn tortillas dipped in a pureed black bean sauce, topped with queso fresco, raw onion, avocado and lime. Removed Brown Rice 56g and Corn 60g; added Corn Tortillas 60g, Queso Fresco 40g, Onion 25g, Garlic 4g, Vegetable Oil 8g (the bean puree is fried and the tortillas warmed in fat); Black Beans 50 -> 70g, Avocado 50 -> 30g, Lime 15 -> 10g. Scaled DOWN from the report's proposed grams (see blocked): its 120g beans / 90g tortillas / 50g queso came to ~923 cal against a ~514 cal original. At these grams the dish is ~623 cal (+21%, inside the band) and protein rises 18 -> 27g, which is the shape shift the report wanted.

steps: Poach the chicken breast in lightly salted water until just cooked through, about 15 minutes, then shred it with two forks and keep a little of the poaching broth.
Blend the tomato with the garlic, chipotle powder, Mexican oregano and cumin until smooth.
Slice half the onion thinly and fry it in the vegetable oil until softened and translucent.

Pour the blended sauce into the pan and cook it down for about 10 minutes until it darkens and thickens, loosening it with a splash of the reserved broth if it tightens too far. Season with salt and black pepper.
Return the shredded chicken to the sauce and simmer 5 minutes so it takes up the tinga.
Warm the corn tortillas on a dry pan and pile the tinga on top.
Finish with the rest of the onion chopped raw, the chopped cilantro and a squeeze of lime.

note: Approved non-dish rebuild, and the name was lying: there was no chipotle in the Chipotle Chicken Bowl - the seasoning was paprika plus chili powder, and chipotle is a specific smoke-dried jalapeno (same class of error as turmeric-for-aji-amarillo in the Peruvian audit). Took the report's strong path: rebuilt as Tinga de Pollo, the Puebla dish that actually IS chicken in chipotle. Removed Brown Rice 52g, Black Beans 27g, Corn 50g, Avocado 40g; added Tomato 120g, Onion 50g, Garlic 5g, Corn Tortillas 80g, Lime 15g, Vegetable Oil 10g. Removed Paprika and Chili Powder; added Chipotle Powder 2g and Mexican Oregano 1g; dropped Garlic Powder now that real garlic is in the list. Kept Chicken Breast rather than the more traditional thigh, and raised it 160 -> 180g with tortillas at 80g rather than the report's 60g, to hold the high-protein tag and stay inside the macro band: ~657 -> ~609 cal, protein 62 -> 62. Also removes one of the slice's three near-identical bowls.

steps: Simmer the black beans until soft in about a cup of water, then drain them, keeping a little of the cooking liquid.

Heat the vegetable oil in a pan and refry the beans with the cumin, mashing them with the back of a spoon and loosening with the reserved liquid until thick and spreadable. Season with salt and black pepper.
Blister the bell pepper and onion over high heat until the skins char in spots, then cut them into strips and toss with the Mexican oregano and the minced jalapeno to make rajas con cebolla.
Warm the whole wheat tortilla in a dry pan until soft and flexible.
Spread the refried beans down the middle of the tortilla, lay the rajas over them and scatter the mozzarella on top.
Roll the burrito tightly, tucking in the sides, then set it seam-side down in the dry pan for a minute or two to seal and melt the cheese.

note: Northern-Mexican rebuild, stays vegetarian, so the Mexican label becomes correct. Removed Brown Rice 40g - rice inside a burrito is the Mission-style (San Francisco, 1960s) marker, not a Juarez one - and removed Avocado 50g, a Cal-Mex guacamole-filling convention. Black Beans 39 -> 90g and refried, which is the traditional-correct lever for the lost calories. Cheddar Cheese 20g -> Mozzarella Cheese 30g as the asadero/Chihuahua stand-in. Added Onion 30g and recast the bell pepper as blistered rajas. Removed Chili Powder; added Mexican Oregano and Jalapeno so there is a real chile. Vegetable Oil 8g added because refried beans require fat. Renamed off the generic menu-category name. ~646 -> ~678 cal, protein 23 -> 31.

steps: Peel and devein the shrimp, then toss them with the lime juice, minced garlic, cumin, Mexican oregano, salt and black pepper and leave them to marinate for 10 minutes.
Slice the bell pepper and onion into strips.
Heat a skillet over high heat and sear the shrimp 2-3 minutes per side, then set them aside.
In the same pan, cook the bell pepper and onion strips for 3-4 minutes until charred at the edges but still crisp.
Warm the tortilla in a dry pan.
Fill the tortilla with the shrimp, peppers and onion, and finish with chopped cilantro.

note: Report's recommended path A: relabel, do not rewrite. Mexican -> Tex-Mex; fajitas are a South Texas ranch dish (faja = the skirt-steak cut itself), popularised by Ninfa's in Houston from 1973, and a shrimp version is a further extension of that restaurant dish. The recipe itself is well built - correct high-heat technique, no phantoms, nothing unused - so ingredients are untouched. Only the seasoning changed: removed Paprika 2g (generic American fajita rub), added Mexican Oregano 1g, and moved the lime and garlic from garnish/last-30-seconds into a proper 10-minute marinade, which is the real Tex-Mex fajita treatment.

Relabel only, per the report's primary fix: Mexican -> Tex-Mex. Same American fast-casual bowl as the Chicken Burrito Bowl; as a bowl it is coherent and well built, so no recipe change. The report's secondary suggestion - retiring one of the three near-identical bowls in favour of a different Mexican dish - is a pool-composition decision outside Phase B scope, and is partly answered anyway since Chipotle Chicken Bowl became Tinga de Pollo.

_summary.notes: No nuts, no olives, no Sumac anywhere. Olive Oil not used - Vegetable Oil is the correct fat for these dishes. MERGE NEEDS TO KNOW: (1) three recipes take the new Tex-Mex label, so that label must exist before merge. (2) Chili Powder is now dropped from all four recipes in this slice that carried it (Chicken Burrito Bowl, Chicken Enchiladas, Veggie Burrito, Chipotle Chicken Bowl) - it is a strong orphan-sweep candidate app-wide; Paprika drops from two here and is a weaker candidate. Both live in RECIPE_SPICE_OVERRIDES, not the registry. (3) Cheddar Cheese drops from all three of its recipes in this slice and BBQ Sauce from one; the report verified BBQ Sauce has 7 references app-wide so it is not orphaned - re-derive Cheddar yourself. (4) Six spice names new to data usage need grocery categories: Chipotle Powder, Mexican Oregano, Guajillo Chile, Ancho Chile, Jalapeno, Epazote. (5) Guajillo Chile 8g and Ancho Chile 4g exceed SPEC's 0.5-3g spice range deliberately - dried whole chiles are the sauce base, and these are the report's own amounts; they carry ~25 cal of real macro that the zero-macro spice model discards, on a ~970 cal dish. (6) Macro moves to expect: Enfrijoladas +21% cal and protein 18 -> 27 (biggest shape change in the slice, worth a validator look); Enchiladas +7% cal, protein -3g; everything else within +/-15%.
